youtube.baslik: Why does a hearing test matter so much in sudden vertigo? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In vestibular neuritis, hearing loss and tinnitus are not expected and the audiogram is normal. If sudden sensorineural hearing loss accompanies vertigo, labyrinthitis or a stroke of the anterior inferior cerebellar artery, or AICA, which can also supply the inner ear, may be considered. Anyone with vertigo and sudden hearing loss is referred for physician evaluation without delay.

cumleler: Why does a hearing test matter so much in sudden vertigo?
In vestibular neuritis, hearing loss and tinnitus are not expected.
In labyrinthitis, inflammation affects the whole inner ear, adding hearing loss.
An anterior inferior cerebellar artery, or AICA, stroke can affect the labyrinth.
Then sudden hearing loss comes together with vertigo.
Vertigo with sudden hearing loss calls for prompt physician evaluation.
